title: Do three to four and seventy two to ninety six match?
description: Two ratios, three to four and seventy two to ninety six, are each reduced to the simplest form and compared. Keeko's doubt is that they cannot match because the gap between the terms is one in the first and twenty four in the second.
teaching_notes: One idea: two ratios are proportional when their simplest forms are the same. Watch for students who compare the gaps between the terms instead of reducing.

video_script.why: The child applies the simplest form test to ratios with larger numbers, where matching by eye does not work.
video_script.substitution: Reduce each ratio by the highest common factor and compare the simplest forms.
video_script.anchor: the two ratios 3 : 4 and 72 : 96 written side by side on the board
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says the ratios are not proportional because the gaps are different, one in three to four and twenty four in seventy two to ninety six. Both terms of three to four are multiplied by twenty four, so the bubble is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: Seventy two to ninety six reduces to three to four, so the two ratios are proportional.

final_answer.spoken: yes, seventy two to ninety six reduces to three to four, so the ratios are proportional

maths_rules: 3 : 4: HCF of 3 and 4 is 1, so it is already in simplest form
72 : 96: HCF of 72 and 96 is 24, since 72 = 24 × 3 and 96 = 24 × 4
the simplest forms are the same, so 3 : 4 :: 72 : 96
Keeko's slip: gaps 4 − 3 = 1 and 96 − 72 = 24 differ, but 3 × 24 = 72 and 4 × 24 = 96
video_script.design: One idea: the same simplest form means proportional. Assumes dividing by the highest common factor. Wrong idea: different gaps mean not proportional. The two ratios stay for the whole video.

<bookmark mark='prop'/>Two ratios with the same simplest form are called proportional.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the ratios are not proportional, because the gaps are different.
<bookmark mark='gap'/>Four take away three is one, and ninety six take away seventy two is twenty four.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But the gap between the terms is not the test.
<bookmark mark='mul'/>Three times twenty four is seventy two, and four times twenty four is ninety six.
<bookmark mark='land'/>Both terms were multiplied by the same factor, so the ratios are proportional.
